story: Go is Google's language, not ours

story: Golang generics proposal has been accepted
text: > I'm thinking of Rob Pike I do not remember him being against generics. He is the one who contacted his former colleague Phil Wadler to help with the theoretical validation of the type parameters proposal. In his talk about the Go 2 draft specifications (back then the proposal was still based on contracts) he was positive that a good design can be found. (*) [VIDEO]

story: Map[string]interface{} in Go: a user's manual
text: > purely for ideological reasons There are no ideological reasons. [LINK] "Generics may well come at some point." [LINK] "A language proposal implementing a form of generic types has been accepted for inclusion in the language. If all goes well it will be available in the Go 1.18 release." One of the language designers explaining the motivation for adding parametric polymorphism to Go: [VIDEO] Explaining the benefits of generics: [LINK] From the Featherweight Go paper: [LINK] "Recently, the Go team mooted a design to extend Go with generics, and Rob Pike wrote Wadler to ask: Would you be interested in helping us get polymorphism right (and/or figuring out what “right” means) for some future version of Go?"
Rob Pike explicitly stated that he really isn't into generics, [VIDEO] (starts here) [VIDEO] (he expresses his opinion here) We haven't made our little heads out of nowhere.
